content:
maria: Quick idea — we need a clearer policy for automatic model-variant fallback when the primary is saturated. Thinking: route by (tier, region) -> fallback list, emit compact telemetry, and give ops a toggle in Console. Anyone object?

kevin: +1 on tier/region routing. one nuance: Dedicated customers often expect strict same-family variants. we should not silently downgrade them to tiny models.

sam: agree. maybe a policy split: for hosted customers use cost-aware fallback (ql8, quantized), for dedicated honor "family_only" by default.

priya: telemetry question: what do we expose? per-tenant per-variant will explode cardinality. i propose aggregated labels: model_family, variant_tier (e.g. full, quant, micro), and tenant_tier. that gives us fallback_rate and avg_fallback_latency without too many series.

maria: exactly. metrics I want: routing.fallback_count{model_family,variant_tier,region,tenant_tier}, routing.fallback_latency_ms (p95), and a boolean routing.fallback_enabled per-tenant.

kevin: UX: in Console show a per-route "Fallback health" sparkline + a table of top fallback pairs (primary -> most used fallback). ability to disable auto-fallback per-route or per-tenant would be handy.

sam: API debate: should we include variant info in response headers (X-Model-Variant) or in response body meta? headers are easy for proxies/caches. body is better for structured SDKs.

priya: header is my vote. also add an opt-in response field: meta.variant for customers who want it in the body. keep header authoritative.

maria: agreed. header naming: X-Redwood-Model-Variant? or X-RW-Model? keep long-form for clarity.

kevin: X-Redwood-Model-Variant sounds fine. but ensure we don't leak internal names for Private deployments — maybe canonicalize to family+class only for public responses.

sam: another operational ask: add a short rate-limited log entry when fallback happens: 1 per 5s per tenant, joinable with request_id so traces can be followed.

maria: adding now to the spec. also a config sketch for routing policy (example):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  name: auto-fallback
  ordered_variants:
    - id: redwood/open-7b
      family: open-7b
      tier: full
    - id: redwood/open-7b-ql8
      family: open-7b
      tier: quant
    - id: redwood/open-3b
      family: open-3b
      tier: micro
  constraints:
    region: match_request_region
    tenant_tier: prefer_same_or_lower_family
  tenant_overrides:
    dedicated:
      enforce_family_only: true
```

priya: how do we make rollout safe? my suggestion: canary by tenant_tier and route percentage. Console toggle to preview which tenants would be affected before enabling globally.

maria: yes — rollout UI should show estimated impacted qps and projected cost delta (we can approximate from historic token usage and fallback token multiplier).

kevin: SLA concern: when primary saturated and we fallback to a cheaper variant, latency might improve but quality may drop. we need to route_quality_metric (eval-set regression) and wire a regression alert if fallback_quality drops below threshold for a tenant.

sam: good call — we already have evals per-promptset. tie eval outcomes to fallback streams so we can surface "quality regressions caused by fallback" in Console.

maria: ops-bot: can you add a ticket for telemetry + header + config schema + console mockups? (reacts :eyes:)

ops-bot: created INC-4721: "auto-variant-fallback telemetry + API header + Console UX" assigned to @kevin, @priya. link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INC-4721

deploy-bot: deploy queued for staging config branch feature/fallback-spec -> staging (build #3189).

priya: action items from thread: 1) schema PR for routing policy (sam) 2) metric names + retention plan (priya) 3) header + SDK change (kevin) 4) Console mocks + rollout UX (maria) 5) canary plan doc (sam). I'll consolidate and create a doc.

maria: thanks. I'll put a short spec in the docs repo and ping infra for needed counters.

kevin: one last note — ensure tenant opt-out API: POST /v1/tenants/:id/config {"auto_fallback": false} so customers can opt out.

maria: noted. closing this thread for now, will link spec when ready.
